android.desc: Looking for a powerful tool to inspect, dissect, and explore your apps? Apk Analyzer shows you everything Android knows about an app — permissions, certificates, components, full manifest, and much more. The most downloaded, trusted, and 100% open-source APK analysis tool on Google Play. 📱 Inspect any app already on your device, or open an .apk file you haven't installed yet, and get the same full report before you install it. 📋 Every App Report Contains: - 🔐 Permissions: Every permission requested, with a plain-language description and protection level. - ✍️ Signing & Certificates: Issuer, subject, validity, fingerprints, and signing-scheme versions. - 🏷️ App Metadata: Package and app name, version, category, install and update dates. - 📶 SDK & Compatibility: Target and minimum Android version, required and optional hardware features. - 🧩 Components Breakdown: Activities, services, broadcast receivers, and content providers — with intent filters and launch options. - 🏬 Install Source: The full install-source chain — which store or app actually installed it. - 📦 Packaging: Native libraries, ABIs, split APKs, and storage size. - 📄 Full Manifest: Decode and view the complete, readable AndroidManifest.xml, and export it directly to your storage. 🧭 Browse by Attribute Turn the question around: which apps request a given permission, which share a signing certificate, which target a given Android version, where each app came from, and which apps share a UID. 🤖 On-Device AI Summary A short, factual, plain-language read on what an app is and what its permissions imply — generated entirely on-device. Nothing about your apps is ever sent anywhere. 📤 Export & Share Save an app's APK or icon to storage, share a text summary, or export the readable manifest — no root required. 🔒 Safe, Open-Source & Private - No root access required. - 100% Ad-Free. - Fully open source, licensed under the GNU General Public License v3 (GPLv3). Take control of the apps on your device. Download Apk Analyzer today.

quotes.text:
Heh, mine's "after I count to infinity twice" :) I can't remember if I cribbed that from somewhere...

IIUC, the permissions apps request ultimately just enable access to certain APIs; they don't do anything on their own: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24858462/how-to-check-if-android-permission-is-actually-being-used (see 1st comment). So apps like https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer and https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ubqsoft.sec01 basically reason about the ceiling of everything an app might use across its lifetime. It's arguably a tad misrepresentative, like seeing a wall of text from a distance can be scary.

Furthermore, the very orthogonal way permissions are categorized relative to internal API architecture is woefully unintuitive at best, making it next to impossible to come up with good summary judgements of what a given app might be trying to do. For example, a given game might want access to your "cell ID information" because the analytics SDK it uses is overly invasive (while the game itself never needs the info), while a smart-device controller app might request "real-time location information" (I forget exactly what the permission is called) just because the smart device happens to use BTLE (Bluetooth LE), because BTLE's fast connect/disconnect characteristics made it ripe for abuse by indoor location tracking systems in shops and whatnot, and so Android had to make that the permission name since it's …
